story.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump to Continue White House Ballroom Construction
story.summary: The US Supreme Court has permitted the continuation of construction on a $400 million ballroom project at the White House, initiated by Trump. However, the court did not make a ruling on the legality of the project. Chief Justice John Roberts expressed dissent, stating that the construction is likely unlawful.

timeline_highlights.title: Court Halts Trump's White House Ballroom Construction, Appeals Expected
timeline_highlights.summary: A federal appeals court has ordered the halt of construction on Donald Trump's planned $400 million ballroom at the White House, stating that such a significant alteration requires congressional approval. The ruling follows a challenge from the National Trust for Historic Preservation and is seen as a test of presidential power. Trump has announced plans to appeal the decision to the Supreme Court.
key_facts: Federal appeals court ordered halt to Trump's ballroom construction.
Court ruled that the project requires congressional approval.
Trump plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court.

timeline_highlights.title: Supreme Court Temporarily Allows Construction of $400 Million White House Ballroom
timeline_highlights.summary: The US Supreme Court has granted a temporary order allowing the continuation of construction on a $400 million ballroom at the White House, a project associated with President Donald Trump. This decision comes after lower courts had previously ordered a halt to the work, citing the need for congressional approval. The ruling provides a temporary victory for the Trump administration as it navigates ongoing legal challenges regarding the renovation.
key_facts: Supreme Court allows construction to continue temporarily.
Project cost is approximately $400 million.
Lower courts had ordered a halt due to lack of congressional approval.

timeline_highlights.title: Supreme Court Permits Continued Construction of $400M White House Ballroom
timeline_highlights.summary: The Supreme Court has temporarily allowed construction of President Trump's White House ballroom to proceed, following a stay issued by Chief Justice John Roberts. This decision comes as the court considers an appeal from the Trump administration regarding the project, which is estimated to cost nearly $400 million and is funded by private donors and companies. The ruling prevents a halt to construction that would have been enforced by lower court decisions.
